correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 circum-incenter simplex, Nour Lemmas 2.1-2.2 verify h<=1/n, all p_i=rho u_i are boundary points, and all M n_j are feasible centers. The gap g(w)-h has isolated linear minima at facet normals since each contact point is in the relative interior of its facet; tangent-slice support lower bounds yield kappa>0. The boundary-points bound implies t<=M and T^2<=f(t)-2rho t(g(w)-h). Subtracting from M^2 gives M-t<=2 epsilon/(1-4h^2), then t>=M/2 and gap<=2epsilon/rho; consequently the stated center bound follows exactly. Inner homothets of an attaining ball prove the exponent one cannot improve. A nonregular tetrahedral calculation and 20,000 finite directions check formulas, but infinite quantified claims rest on written inequalities.

value.rationale: For the nonconvex finite-ball counterexamples that establish sharpness of the universal interior-sphere constant, maximal radius alone does not quantify geometric behavior of a nearly maximal containing ball. This theorem recovers a finite facet-labeled optimizer set and supplies a global sharp Lipschitz-type recovery estimate for all admissible centers. Such stability is a natural robust inverse question about geometric extremizers and is not a renamed radius computation; it applies to nonregular families in every dimension and pinpoints the best possible rate.
